title: Tuna white bean lemon pasta
description: Tender penne, flaky tuna and creamy beans with lemon, parsley and sweet cherry tomatoes.
ingredients: 2 cans (5 ounces each) chunk light tuna in water, drained
1 can (15 ounces) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the penne and cook according to its package, usually 10 to 12 minutes; reserve 1 cup cooking water before draining.
While the water heats, warm the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Cook garlic for 30 seconds, then add tomatoes, salt and pepper. Cook 6 minutes until several tomatoes burst.
Add the beans and 1/2 cup pasta water; simmer 3 minutes. Fold in the tuna without breaking all the flakes.

Add pasta, lemon zest, half the lemon juice and parsley. Toss over low heat for 1 minute, adding reserved water a tablespoon at a time until lightly glossy. Taste before adding remaining lemon juice; divide into equal servings.
notes: A pantry pasta built around lemony beans rather than the creamy baked sauce of tuna casserole. Tomatoes supply a vegetable component without a second side. Hands-on estimate: 18 minutes. For eight servings, use two pans of the stated size or cook two batches; keep food depth and piece sizes unchanged. Do not double cooking times. Check packaged ingredients for allergens. title: Tuna egg white bean dinner salad
description: Tuna flakes, firm-yolk eggs and white beans in a crunchy cucumber-tomato salad with mustard dressing.
ingredients: 2 cans (5 ounces each) chunk light tuna in water, drained
2 cans (15 ounces each) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Place eggs in a medium saucepan with cold water to cover. Bring to a boil, cover, remove from heat and stand 12 minutes. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter; yolks should be firm.
While eggs stand, whisk mustard, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper in a large serving bowl. Add beans, cucumber, tomatoes and scallions and toss.
Flake tuna into large pieces and fold through the beans. Toast bread while the eggs cool.
Divide bean salad among serving plates and top each with an equal share of the eggs. Serve one slice of toast each, leaving the egg pieces intact rather than mashing them into the dressing.
notes: Eggs and white beans make a pantry tuna salad into a complete dinner without mayonnaise. Fresh vegetables remain crunchy, and the simple mustard vinaigrette is mixed before the fish is folded in. Hands-on estimate: 18 minutes. For eight servings, use two pans of the stated size or cook two batches; keep food depth and piece sizes unchanged. Do not double cooking times. Check packaged ingredients for allergens. title: Pork shrimp cabbage noodle skillet
description: Savory noodles with browned pork, tender shrimp and cabbage in a mild ginger sauce.
ingredients: 8 ounces large raw shrimp, peeled, deveined and thawed
1 bag (12 ounces) shredded cabbage and carrot slaw
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook noodles according to their package. Drain well. Mix soy sauce, vinegar, honey, sesame oil and the measured water in a cup.
Heat neutral oil in a large wok over medium-high. Add pork and cook 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned and at least 160°F.
Add cabbage-carrot slaw and cook 3 minutes. Stir in garlic, ginger and shrimp and cook 3 to 4 minutes until shrimp is pearly and opaque, tossing to expose all sides.
Add noodles and sauce. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and evenly coated, then divide among serving plates. Serve immediately while cabbage retains a little bite.
notes: A small amount of browned pork supplies richness while shrimp provides a second texture. Bagged cabbage and carrot reduce preparation, and the sauce is intentionally mild rather than chili-heavy. Hands-on estimate: 20 minutes.
